use_when: To trigger a primary action, such as submitting a form or confirming a choice.
When the action is a single, clear next step the user should take.
For calls-to-action that need visual emphasis — use the filled/primary style.
For secondary or less prominent actions — use the outline style instead of a second filled button.
To open a modal, drawer, or another view, when the action is not a navigation link.
For destructive actions (e.g. delete, remove), paired with the error/danger state.
Inside forms, toolbars, cards, and dialogs — wherever a discrete, tappable action is needed.

dont_use_when.when: For navigation between pages or views — use a Link component instead.
When more than one primary action competes for attention on the same screen — keep only one primary button per view.
As a label or static status indicator — use a Badge/Lozenge component instead.
For a toggleable on/off state — use a Toggle or Checkbox component instead.

variant_intent.error: For destructive actions (e.g. delete, remove), paired with the error/danger state. Reserve the error/outline-error state for destructive or blocking actions only.
variant_intent.outline: For secondary or less prominent actions — use the outline style instead of a second filled button.
variant_intent.outline error: Reserve the error/outline-error state for destructive or blocking actions only.

a11y.fact: Renders a native <button> element with type="button".
Accepts native button attributes (including aria-* and disabled) and spreads them onto the <button>.
The default icon is decorative: rendered as with alt="".
The visible label is rendered as text content inside the button, giving it its accessible name.
Keyboard focus shows a 2px solid outline with a 2px offset on :focus-visible.
